home.title: Toile Blanche | Saint-Paul de Vence
home.description: 22 suites, two restaurants, and a contemporary art collection in Saint-Paul de Vence. A declared artwork by the Leroy Brothers on the Côte d'Azur.
home.heroSecond: The art is not on the walls, it is the walls.
home.heroBody: And the particular pleasure of going nowhere for a few days.
home.storyP1: The Leroy Brothers arrived in Saint-Paul de Vence in 2004 with three rooms and a long-term view.
home.storyP2: Over twenty years, they bought the neighbouring houses one by one — from neighbours who became friends. Then, when the time was right, they stopped and built the version they had always had in mind.
home.storyP3: The result is something genuinely difficult to categorise.
home.storyP4: 22 suites. Two restaurants. Lots of sculptures. Three pools. 20,000m² of gardens. Saint-Paul de Vence.
home.feelingP1: Toile Blanche sits on the edge of Saint-Paul de Vence — the village that gave the world Fondation Maeght, that sheltered Picasso, Chagall and Calder — and it takes that responsibility seriously.
home.feelingP2: But not seriously in the way that makes you feel watched. The pool is warm. The rosé is cold. The art will make you stop and think, and then you will go back to the pool.
home.artDesc: In 2026, Toile Blanche was declared a work of art — by the people who built it. The Leroy Brothers are a Belgian collective working at the edge of post-internet art since 1997. They are also, now, the architects and curators of this place. The collection they have assembled spans painting, sculpture, photography and installation. Some pieces were made for specific rooms. Others arrived because there was nowhere else they belonged.
home.artDesc2: It is a living collection. New work arrives each season. Staying here more than once means a different conversation with the same walls.
home.tablesDesc: La Guinguette is lunch under the plane trees — rosé, grilled fish, the specific joy of eating outside in Provence. Le Restaurant is the evening version: more considered, more intimate, the kitchen at full attention. Both menus are built around what is in season, what is local, what is honest.
home.lifeDesc: Saint-Paul de Vence is three minutes on foot. Fondation Maeght is five. Beyond that — studio visits, the Art Route, the valley on a bicycle, and the particular pleasure of doing none of it.

home.newsletterDesc: Not too often. Just enough. The occasional note from Saint-Paul de Vence — new arrivals in the collection, what is on the table this season, and the things worth knowing before you visit.

theProperty.title: The Property | Toile Blanche | Saint-Paul de Vence
theProperty.description: Saint-Paul de Vence sits on a ridge above the valley. The village has been watching the light do this for a long time. So have we.
theProperty.cluster1Text: Saint-Paul de Vence sits on a ridge above the valley. The village has been watching the light do this for a long time. So have we.
theProperty.cluster2Text: Seven buildings. Two centuries of stone.
theProperty.cluster3Text: Each suite is different. The light in the Cabanat arrives from the valley. In the Artiste it comes through two-hundred-year-old stone. The Pénéquet has a pool and no particular agenda.
theProperty.cluster4Text: Three pools for everyone. Four more that are entirely yours. Heated from mid-April, when the season decides it is ready.
theProperty.cluster5Text: The tomatoes arrived this morning. The wine list is a declaration of love for the region. Lunch lasts as long as it should.
theProperty.cluster6Text: In 2026, Toile Blanche was declared a work by the Leroy Brothers. Toile Blanche continues to operate normally.
theProperty.cluster7Text: 20,000m² of Provençal gardens. Wild rosemary, century-old olive trees, and a sculpture trail that changes each season. Designed not to be looked at, but lived in.
theProperty.cluster8Text: The light changes. The stone holds the warmth. Some days you notice nothing. Others, everything.
